title: Graphite VerificationResult
description: Output of the Graphite verification pipeline. Field parity with graphite-core/src/verification.rs VerificationResult and the TypeScript/Go SDKs. SECURITY CONTRACT (Round 30): sign only when `executable` is true (decision == 'executable_approved'). `approved` says whether the pipeline refused the transaction; it never said whether the transaction may be signed — an approval from a node without an RPC rests on static analysis and carries `not_simulated`, and a descriptive approval binds to no bytes. `decision` is computed by the Core from `approved`, `risk_verdict`, `policy_verdict`, `scope` and `layers` (see its description) and SDKs recompute and cross-check it. confidence, policy_verdict, risk_verdict and trust_tier are evidence for audit and explanation, never a gate. `scope` says WHAT was verified: scope.kind == 'artifact_bound' means the verdict covers the exact transaction bytes supplied, subject to scope.unobserved; 'descriptive' means it covers only caller-supplied metadata and nothing constrains what is actually signed; `scope` is required: a payload without it (a pre-2026-09-08 server) does not satisfy this schema and must be treated as unknown rather than as either answer. A transport error, timeout or non-200 means verification did not happen: a hard stop, never an implicit pass.

approved.description: Whether the pipeline refused the transaction (false) or not (true). NOT permission to sign: gate on `executable`. Kept with its old meaning for compatibility.

decision.description: Round 30 (G-01). What this verdict permits. ONLY `executable_approved` permits signing: approved, bound to the exact bytes (scope.kind == 'artifact_bound'), simulated by Graphite (scope.simulated), no unobserved code beyond the inherent `program_semantics` and `inner_instructions`, risk Clear, policy Approved, and no layer `failed`. `analysis_only` is an approval on less evidence than execution needs (descriptive scope, not simulated, no state diff, unresolved lookup tables, caller-supplied privileges, a failed layer report) — every approval from a node without an RPC is analysis_only. `inconclusive` is a refusal whose only risk findings are `VerificationIncomplete` (evidence could not be obtained). `blocked` is every other refusal. SDKs recompute this rule from the verdict's own fields and treat a disagreement, or a value not listed here, as not executable.

executable.description: Round 30 (G-01). True iff decision == 'executable_approved'. THE field to gate signing on — `approved` alone never meant 'safe to sign': without an RPC nothing is simulated and an approval carries `not_simulated`.

policy_verdict.description: Evidence, not a gate. The Core emits exactly "Approved" when `approved` is true and "Rejected" otherwise (verification.rs folds the final risk status in, so the two can never disagree); the root's if/then/else enforces that pairing.

content_hash.description: DEPRECATED name (Round 30, R-M10); read `instruction_bind_key`, which carries the same value. A 64-bit identifier of the described INSTRUCTION (framed SHA-256 over program, discriminator, accounts, data and CPI targets, truncated): the key audit and lifecycle records bind to. NOT the transaction's identity — that is scope.transaction_sha256 — and not collision-resistant. Kept for one minor version.

instruction_bind_key.description: Round 30 (R-M10). The same value as `content_hash`, under a name that says what it is: the 64-bit key binding audit and lifecycle records to the described instruction. The transaction's identity is scope.transaction_sha256.

instruction_count.description: Always 1: the summary covers the described instruction only.

compute_budget_units.description: A heuristic ESTIMATE (base + per account + per declared CPI), never a measurement. What the bytes request is scope.compute_budget; what a simulation consumed is reported by L3.

transaction.description: A SUMMARY of the one described instruction (Rust: InstructionSummary) — not a transaction and not wire bytes: no fee payer, no blockhash, no signatures, no sibling instructions. The bytes a verdict binds to are the caller's artifact, identified by scope.transaction_sha256.

name.description: The account slot's name in the manifest (e.g. source, authority). Omitted when empty: an account past the manifest's declared list, or of an unknown program.

identity.description: How this account's identity was verified. Unverified means genuinely externally-determined (no PDA formula, no fixed constant) — disclosed honestly rather than assumed safe.

expected_address_mismatch.description: A manifest-declared fixed-constant slot (e.g. the SPL Token program) did not match the supplied address — a substitution attempt. Hard-blocks approval.

privilege_mismatch.description: A caller-supplied real AccountMeta disagreed with the manifest in a security-relevant direction: a required signer that is not actually signed, or a manifest-readonly slot marked writable. Hard-blocks approval.

program_upgrades.description: Roadmap R-M1: programs this transaction invokes whose deployment changed (redeployed, or handed to a new upgrade authority) since Graphite last saw them, read from the BPF Upgradeable Loader with an RPC attached. Absent when none did. Reported, not refused, unless the operator set GRAPHITE_QUARANTINE_ON_UPGRADE (then `quarantined` is true and the verdict is blocked as a quarantined program).

items.description: One pipeline layer. `status` is the tri-state truth and `passed` is derived from it: true exactly when status is "passed" (GAP-2026-08-06-3).

scope.description: What this verdict is BOUND to, and what it did not observe. This is the field that makes Graphite's central promise checkable rather than assumed: the thing it approved is the thing that gets signed and executed, and every security-relevant property of that thing was either independently verified or explicitly identified as unverified. `approved` alone does not say which half applies — a verdict describing caller-supplied metadata and one bound to real signed bytes are otherwise the same shape. An execution gate that can move funds should require kind == 'artifact_bound' rather than gating on `approved` alone. Required: the Core has emitted it on every verdict since 2026-09-08. A payload without it is not a valid v1 result and must be treated as unknown, never as 'descriptive'. ENFORCED SHAPE: the two kinds are separate schemas, not one object with optional fields. A payload claiming kind == 'artifact_bound' without transaction_sha256, transaction_bytes and simulated is INVALID — previously it validated, because those fields were described as 'artifact_bound only' in prose and required nowhere, so the one field a consumer is told to gate execution on could be asserted without the evidence that gives it meaning (found by review 2026-09-11).

oneOf.title: artifact_bound
oneOf.description: Bound to exact transaction bytes. Every field here is intrinsic to that binding and is therefore required: a binding without the digest of what was bound is not a binding.

transaction_sha256.description: artifact_bound only. SHA-256 of the exact transaction bytes supplied, so a caller can recompute it over what it is about to submit and refuse if it differs. A stronger binding than content_hash, which covers a projection of one instruction and cannot see the fee payer, the blockhash, the signer set, or any sibling instruction.

transaction_bytes.description: artifact_bound only. Length of the supplied artifact.

simulated.description: artifact_bound only. Whether a simulator actually executed those bytes. False means the artifact was hashed but never run, so the verdict still rests on static analysis of the described instruction.

unobserved.description: Security-relevant properties Graphite did not independently establish, stated as what is missing rather than as caveats about the checks. Never empty: claiming to have observed everything is a strong assertion that must be argued for, not fall out of an empty list.

unobserved_codes.description: unobserved_codes[i] names unobserved[i]: same length, same order. The stable identifiers a consumer decides on. `program_semantics` and `inner_instructions` are inherent to every artifact-bound verdict; every other code names an observation that was possible and did not happen, and an execution-capable integration MUST NOT execute on a verdict carrying one it has not explicitly accepted (the SAK bridge's ResidualPolicy refuses them by default). Same length as `unobserved`: JSON Schema cannot state that two arrays are equally long, so the SDK validators (validateVerificationResult, DecodeVerificationResult) enforce it.

message_version.description: The message version the supplied bytes carry, read from them (Round 24). Absent when the bytes did not parse, and from servers before Round 24.

compute_budget.description: artifact_bound only, Round 21. What the transaction asks of the runtime's compute budget, read from its bytes: the v1 header, or the Compute Budget program's instructions for legacy and v0. Absent when the bytes could not be parsed. `priority_fee_lamports` is the priority fee the fee payer pays (at most this, when no limit is set); a request above the plausible-fee ceiling is refused with risk pattern ExcessivePriorityFee.

problems.description: What the runtime would refuse: a duplicated or malformed Compute Budget instruction, a heap request outside its rules.

oneOf.title: descriptive
oneOf.description: No transaction bytes were supplied, so there is nothing to bind to and the artifact fields must NOT appear. Their presence alongside kind == descriptive would suggest a binding that does not exist.

unobserved.description: Security-relevant properties Graphite did not independently establish, stated as what is missing rather than as caveats about the checks. Never empty: claiming to have observed everything is a strong assertion that must be argued for, not fall out of an empty list.

The stable identifiers a consumer decides on. `program_semantics` and `inner_instructions` are inherent to every artifact-bound verdict; every other code names an observation that was possible and did not happen, and an execution-capable integration MUST NOT execute on a verdict carrying one it has not explicitly accepted (the SAK bridge's ResidualPolicy refuses them by default).
